REPUBLIC OF SEYCHELLES 
MINISTRY OF FOREIGN AFFAIRS AND TOURISM 
FOREIGN AFFAIRS DEPARTMENT 
 
 
Victoria, 21 April 2023 
Communiqué  
 
Manual extension of Passports for Seychellois citizens residing abroad 
 
The Government of Seychelles, through its Immigration and Civil Status Department, will 
begin issuing a manual renewal in the Seychelles Ordinary Passports for Seychellois citizens 
living abroad who cannot renew their expiring Passports. This follows the introduction of 
biometric passports last year, requiring applicants to be physically present at the only Passport 
Issuing Office in Victoria, Seychelles. 
The manual renewal will be endorsed on page three of the Passport and will be valid for a 
maximum of three years from the expiry date of the Passport. All non-biometric Ordinary 
Passports shall be phased out by 2027.  
This service has no application fee, and applicants must forward their Passports with an 
explanatory note to Passport Office in Victoria, Seychelles.  
Passports for extension should be forwarded to: 
Passport Officer 
Immigration Division  
Immigration and Civil Status Department  
Independence House  
Victoria  
Seychelles 
 
Tel: (+248) 429 36 26  
Email: gfrancoise@gov.sc 
Seychellois citizens with expired Passports still have recourse to an Emergency Travel 
Document (ETD) issued by Seychelles’ Diplomatic and Consular Missions.   
Additional information or queries can be directed to the Diaspora unit at diaspora@mfa.gov.sc 
END

### Government Targets Introduction of Digital Human Resource Management System in 2027

### 14 October 2026 |

The government is aiming to begin implementing a digital Human Resource Management System (HRMS) next year as part of wider efforts to reduce administrative delays, improve efficiency and strengthen public service delivery, Vice-President Mr Sebastien Pillay said.

The Vice-President outlined this expectation during a strategic briefing with representatives of FreeBalance at State House this afternoon, where discussions centred on the government's digital transformation agenda and its vision for a more modern, efficient and technologically driven public service.

In his introductory remarks, Vice-President Pillay stressed that digital transformation must deliver tangible improvements in the way government institutions operate, particularly by reducing the time taken to complete administrative processes.

He highlighted the need to eliminate unnecessary delays between processes, explaining that efficiency should be measured not only by the availability of digital systems but also by how quickly services can be delivered.

The Vice-President acknowledged that Seychelles, despite its small size, has faced challenges in advancing digitalisation at the desired pace. He emphasised that introducing new technology must be accompanied by changes in existing administrative structures and procedures.

Central to this transformation is the HRMS, which is expected to modernise human resource management across the public service and encourage the digitalisation of other interconnected government processes.

Vice-President Pillay explained that simply converting physical documents into digital formats would not be sufficient if the administrative processes behind them continued to depend heavily on manual intervention.

He noted that while the initial stages of digital transformation may still require officers to manually enter and verify information, the longer-term objective is to establish more integrated systems capable of reducing repetitive administrative tasks.

The Vice-President also addressed concerns surrounding the impact of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, on employment within the public service.

# Cabinet approves new accounting manual for government departments and ministries |01 July 2019

Ms Marengo

A new accounting manual for use by government ministries and departments has been approved by the cabinet of ministers.

The manual, which has been drawn up by the Ministry of Finance, Trade, Investment and Economic Planning, makes provisions for the latest developments and reforms in public finance which have been implemented recently, and which were not covered by the previous manual.

Furthermore, the document establishes new procedures to address challenges highlighted by the auditor general’s report.

Chief accountant of the Treasury, May Paul Marengo, explained that the new manual is to replace the previous one and to document the procedures for use by ministries and accounts departments as a reference and training material.

“The main changes included in the manual is the inclusion of more chapters, for instance on the budget with the new budget that is coming, the manual helps to supplement the guidelines that were established before in terms of how the budget is prepared, how changes within the budget over the course of the budget year is implemented,” Ms Marengo noted.
